newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: IMF sees extended fund facility for Argentina.
newsitem.headline: IMF sees extended fund facility for Argentina.

text.p: IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus said Sunday he reached a tentative agreement to provide an extended fund facility to Argentina and praised government efforts to loosen labour laws and cut the deficit.

"This three-year program will take effect in September 1997 when the current accord expires and it will be used to complete the process of modernization in Argentina," Camdessus was quoted as telling local news agencies after meeting with President Carlos Menem.

In addition, the top aide to Economy Minister Roque Fernandez, Carlos Rodriguez, told reporters that the government and the IMF will have agreed by Wednesday or Thursday "at the latest" on a letter of intent outlining the administration's economic goals.
"At the end of next week I will be recommending that the IMF board give its blessing to the economic goals," Camdessus said.
He also estimated that economic growth would be five percent next year. Argentina's Economy Ministry has predicted three percent growth in 1996.
"We are very confident in the situation of the country," said Camdessus, backing government plans to make labour laws more flexible and to reduce the deficit.
The government has announced programmes to increase taxes and reduce worker benefits, without which, authorities warn, the deficit could hit $6.6 billion this year.
